title: A Chapter of Death, a Man of Grace

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: After Noah was 500 years old, he became the father of Shem, Ham and Japheth. - Gen 5:32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The long genealogy closes with Noah and his three sons - Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Through these three, the whole earth would be repopulated after the flood. The chapter that has beaten out the sad refrain "and then he died" over and over now rests on a note of hope, on the family through whom God would preserve the human race.

This is how God works. Even in a chapter dominated by death, He is quietly preparing rescue. Judgement was coming upon a corrupt world, but grace was already in place. Before the flood is ever mentioned, God has raised up Noah and his sons. Mercy always runs ahead of judgement.

The very next chapter will tell us that "Noah found favor in the eyes of the Lord" (Gen 6:8). That word "favor" is grace - undeserved kindness. In a world ripe for judgement, God set His grace upon one man and his family, and through them preserved His promise of a coming Saviour.

The same God who prepared an ark of rescue for Noah has prepared a greater rescue for us in Christ. In a world under judgement for sin, God offers refuge to all who come to Him by faith. The chapter of death ends by pointing to the hope of salvation - and that hope has a name, Jesus.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Can you see how God prepares grace even before judgement?
- Have you taken refuge in God's provided rescue, Jesus Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Gracious God, thank You that even in a world under judgement, You prepare rescue for those who trust You. Thank You for the refuge I have found in Jesus. Keep me safe in Him.
